title: An Eventown Result for Multisets
summary: We study an extension of the Eventown problem of sets to multisets on $[n] = \{1,2,...,n\}$. A multiset is called $m$-bounded if each element has multiplicity at most $m$. The intersection of two multisets is defined as the multiset in which each element has multiplicity equal to the minimum of its multiplicities in the two original multisets. A family of $m$-bounded multisets is called an Eventown family if every member and the intersection of every pair of distinct members has even cardinality, with cardinalities counted with multiplicities.
